title: Similar Figures: Ratios Within and Between Shapes
seo_title: Grade 7 Similar Figures Worksheets: Scale Factor and Missing Sides (TEKS 7.5A, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.5A generalize the critical attributes of similarity, including ratios within and between similar shapes; 7.5C solve mathematical and real-world problems involving similar shape and scale drawings
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.5A and 7.5C: similar figures, ratios within and between shapes, scale factor, missing sides, angles and perimeter. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Scale factor = big side ÷ matching small side.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Similar figures have the same shape: matching angles are equal and matching sides are proportional.
  • The ratio between shapes (big side ÷ matching small side) is the scale factor.
  • The ratio within one shape (length : width) is the same in both shapes.
  • Perimeters change by the scale factor too.

Examples

Example

5 ft by 8 ft rectangle; similar one has short side 15 ft.

Scale factor 15 ÷ 5 = 3

8 × 3

Answer: 24 ft

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplying5 → 15 is × 3, not + 10.
Matching the wrong sidesMatch shortest with shortest and longest with longest.
Thinking angles change with sizeSimilar shapes have equal angles.

faq.a: Generalize the critical attributes of similarity, including ratios within and between similar shapes.
Solve mathematical and real-world problems involving similar shape and scale drawings.
Yes. All their angles are 90° and their sides are always in the ratio 1 : 1.

faq.q: Do similar shapes have the same area?
faq.a: No. Area changes by the scale factor squared.

items.q: Rectangle P is 10 cm by 8 cm. Rectangle Q is similar, and its length is 25 cm. What is the ratio of length to width in rectangle Q?
items.e: Similar shapes have the same ratio within each shape: length : width = 10 : 8 in both.

items.q: Two similar triangles have matching sides 8 m and 32 m. What is the ratio of the sides of the small triangle to the big triangle?
items.e: 8 : 32 = 1 : 4. This ratio between the shapes is the scale factor.

items.q: Triangle 1 has sides 3, 4 and 5. A similar Triangle 2 has a side of 6 that matches the side of 3. What is the length in Triangle 2 that matches the side of 5?
items.e: Scale factor = 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Multiply: 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: Leo says a 2 × 3 rectangle and a 4 × 5 rectangle are similar because he added 2 to each side. Is he right?
c: No, you must multiply, not add
items.e: 4/2 = 2 but 5/3 ≠ 2: no, you must multiply, not add.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 50° and 60°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 40° and 70°. Triangle 2 has angles 70° and 40°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 70° and 70°. Triangle 1: 40°, 70°, 70°. Triangle 2: 70°, 40°, 70°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 35° and 90°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?
items.e: Similar triangles have equal angles. The third angle is 180° − 35° − 90° = 55°.

items.q: Triangle 1 has angles 50° and 60°. Triangle 2 has angles 50° and 75°. Are they similar?
items.e: Find the third angles: 70° and 55°. Triangle 1: 50°, 60°, 70°. Triangle 2: 50°, 75°, 55°. No, the angles are different.

items.q: Why are two triangles with two equal angles always similar?
c: The third angles must also be equal
items.e: Angles add to 180°, so the third angles match too: the third angles must also be equal.

items.q: Two triangles are similar. One has angles 72° and 48°. What is the third angle of the other triangle?

items.e: Find the third angles: 60° and 30°. Triangle 1: 90°, 30°, 60°. Triangle 2: 60°, 90°, 30°. Yes, by angle-angle (AA).

items.q: A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts off a small triangle. Is the small triangle similar to the big one?
items.e: Parallel lines make equal corresponding angles: yes, they share angles.

items.e: Both have 90° and 30° (so also 60°): AA. Yes.

items.e: Each side is multiplied by 3, so the perimeter is 28 × 3 = 84 in.

items.q: A door is 2 m tall and 0.8 m wide. A model door is 10 cm tall. How wide is it?

items.q: Two similar cylinders: one is twice as tall. How many times as much area does a matching face have?
